phase_note: Amendments 1 and 2 reopened this implemented spec at the requirements phase. Amendment 1 revises Requirements 1 and 7 and adds 10-12; Amendment 2 withdraws the withdrawn methodology, retiring Requirements 4, 5, 6 and 12, revising 1, 2, 3, 9 and 10, and adding Requirement 13 for the withdrawal itself. design.md was regenerated 2026-07-25 against both amendments (result contract redefined, arbitration, superseded-format recognition, the withdrawn methodology's removal). tasks.md was regenerated 2026-07-25 against both amendments, superseding the shipped first pass's plan: 6 major tasks / 17 sub-tasks covering the withdrawal, the redefined contract and payload v2, the [load] settings table and arbitration, the reworked load pass and command surface, documentation, and validation. Three deviations from design.md's migration graph were made for executability, each recorded in the tasks.md preamble: the withdrawn methodology's withdrawal is split into repin-then-delete and sequenced FIRST rather than last (redefining LoadResult breaks the shipped calculator, so no ordering with the deletion last is green); the result-type redefinition and payload v2 are one task (the payload is the type's serialization); and the LOAD_KEYS rename, DOC_VERSION bump and golden regeneration are an explicit cross-boundary integration task (task 2.4). Amendment 3 (2026-07-25) reopened the spec a third time after a cross-spec consistency review, WITHOUT reopening committed work: tasks 1.1-1.3 and 2.1-2.3 are shipped (commits 8a8f008, 7ae2ade, 6386361, 4396c45, c686ae4, 2c5cbaa) and none is rewritten. It revises Requirement 3.1, adds criteria 1.12-1.15 and adds Requirement 14 (the [load] configuration surface), pinning src/fitdocs/load/settings.py as this spec's with a contractual reader surface and total field defaulting; moving the [load] read into apply_load and deleting its default_calculator parameter; adding LoadContext(activity_date, settings) to LoadCalculator.compute while reverting ProfileView to a pure store view; renaming NotConfirmed to NotComputed; and adding LoadCalculator.supports(activity). requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md were amended in place on 2026-07-25 (no regeneration): 68 criteria (was 58), 17 leaf tasks (was 16, new task 3.3 for the contract repin), and the internal dependency order becomes settings -> types -> registry -> ... The canonical test module for the reader is pinned as tests/load/test_settings.py. CORRECTION (2026-07-25, cross-spec import-direction ruling; applied in place, no committed work reopened -- tasks 1.1-1.3 and 2.1-2.4 stand, 2.4 landed as a782034): Amendment 3's move of load/settings.py BELOW load/types.py is WITHDRAWN, along with its justification that settings.py has no fitdocs.load.* imports. That justification was false -- LoadSettings aggregates three sibling specs' typed sub-settings, each in its own load module (SufficiencySettings in load/channels/types.py, ChannelPriority in load/priority.py, FlagSettings in load/qa/types.py) -- and the resulting cycle (types -> settings -> qa/__init__ -> qa/flags -> types partial) was reproduced experimentally on EVERY entry point, because load/__init__.py:17 imports registry which imports types. The ruling: types.py names LoadSettings under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` only, so settings.py returns ABOVE types.py, the internal order is types -> registry -> arbitrate -> ... with types -> {channels/*, priority, qa/*} -> settings -> engine, every sub-package may import load.types freely, and activity-qa-flags deletes its lazy __getattr__ workaround in load/qa/__init__.py (rejected on evidence: it failed on one added future edge). Verified safe: load/types.py:26 already has `from __future__ import annotations`, LoadContext stays constructible with its field type a string, and nothing in the suite calls typing.get_type_hints. Requirement 14 gains criterion 14.7 (69 criteria, was 68; leaf-task count unchanged -- the plan holds 18 leaves, so Amendment 3's '17' undercounted by one): settings sits above the contract module, the contract module's reference to it is type-checking-only, and no package initializer beneath fitdocs.load may eagerly import a module reaching settings -- guarded by extending tests/test_public_api.py's fresh-interpreter subprocess import check, the only test that can catch a re-inversion. requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md amended in place (design: dependency direction, the activity-qa-flags conformance row, LoadContracts and LoadSettings dependency blocks, LoadContext interface, a new revalidation trigger; tasks: 3.1's direction bullet corrected, 3.3 gains the TYPE_CHECKING import and the one-sentence load/types.py docstring amendment, 5.2 gains the plugin-api surface-list reconciliation, 6.4 gains the fresh-interpreter guard). DESIGN RE-VALIDATION (2026-07-25, /kiro-validate-design over the whole amended spec; applied in place, no committed work reopened -- tasks 1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.4 and 3.1 stand). Verdict GO, conditional on three defects, ALL in pending work and none touching a requirement number or a criterion: (1) task 4.1 depended on contract.document_date, which resolves nowhere in src/ or tests/, while the coordination table deferred it to whichever of this spec and athlete-benchmarks lands first -- athlete-benchmarks is at tasks-generated with zero committed tasks, so this spec lands first and task 4.1 now ADDS the accessor, with its boundary extended to DocumentContract as a declared incursion (the same treatment 2.4 was given for the same module); (2) arbitration's no-default branch filtered candidates by declared modality while Reqs 1.6 and 10.2 are both written in terms of the activity's SPORT, so two calculators declaring Modality.OTHER -- the declaration threshold-load must make to reach Walk and Hike -- would resolve a Rowing document to Ambiguous, directing the user to configure a default that cannot help, where Reqs 7.7 and 10.5 require the honest unsupported state; arbitrate now takes the activity and narrows the no-default candidate set by supports(activity) after the registry's modality prefilter, with the forced and configured paths left sport-blind as before; (3) task 6.4's Req 14.7 import guard named `import fitdocs.load.qa`, a package activity-qa-flags creates and which does not exist here, so the final quality gate would red with ModuleNotFoundError the day it was written -- the guard now DISCOVERS the load package's sub-packages instead of naming them, which also means no sibling spec has to edit it. Sequencing consequence: task 3.2 calls supports(), which task 3.3 adds, so 3.2 gains a dependency on 3.3 and loses its (P) marker; it loses nothing in practice because the concurrency it was granted was with major task 2, now committed in full. Leaf-task count unchanged at 18; criteria unchanged at 69. Files amended in place: design.md (Req 14.7 invariant, coordination table, athlete-benchmarks conformance row, contract.py modified-files entry, contract.py sequencing paragraph, arbitration precedence diagram, traceability rows 1.6 and 10.2, the whole Arbitration component incl. signature and postconditions, LoadContracts' supported_modalities note, the supports revalidation trigger, LoadEngine's arbitrate and activity_date notes, arbitration unit-test list), tasks.md (new re-validation preamble, 3.2 rewritten, 4.1 bullets 1 and 3 plus boundary, 6.1 gains the two-broad-modality case, 6.4's guard corrected). SIGNATURE PIN QUALIFIED (2026-07-26, queue item 2026-07-25-document-date-signature-pin; no requirement, criterion, task or component changes, so no re-approval): the cross-spec pin for the document-date accessor instructed whichever spec lands first to add it 'with that exact signature', but every training-load copy wrote it as `document_date(frontmatter) -> date | None`, omitting the PARAMETER type. src/fitdocs/contract.py ships both conventions with the non-optional `Mapping[str, object]` dominant (4 readers to 1), so an implementer of task 4.1 following the majority would have written the non-optional form -- a defensible reading that passes its own review -- while contract.parse_frontmatter returns `dict[str, object] | None` and load/engine.py holds exactly that optional mapping at both call sites, which is also what athlete-benchmarks task 5.2 threads in. All four markdown sites now read `document_date(frontmatter: Mapping[str, object] | None) -> date | None`, character-identical to wiki-contract/design.md:84 and athlete-benchmarks/design.md:172,1085: tasks.md:228 and design.md:315,529 as the queue item specified, plus tasks.md:352, a fourth copy of the same pin in the cross-spec-coordination section that would have re-introduced the drift. NOTE: the 2026-07-25 design-re-validation entry in `amendments` below still quotes the abbreviated form; it is left verbatim because those entries are dated records of what was ruled at the time, and design.md/tasks.md are authoritative for the signature an implementer follows. SUPPORT-QUESTION CALL SHAPE CORRECTED (2026-07-26, queue item 2026-07-26-supports-call-shape-design-drift, closed; no requirement, criterion, task or component changes, so no re-approval). Amendment 3 specified the support question as LoadCalculator.supports(activity) with a default supplied as a body on the Protocol. Both halves are unimplementable in Python and fail independently: a Protocol method body is inherited only by explicit subclasses, so a duck-typed calculator never receives the default; and declaring the member at all makes it mandatory for structural conformance, contradicting criterion 1.14. Task 3.3 shipped the resolution in code (7f10234) -- the module-level supports_activity(calculator, activity) in load/types.py, using a calculator's own supports when it defines one and falling back to modality membership otherwise -- but left design.md unamended, since the spec directory lay outside that task's boundary. design.md is now amended at all 12 affected sites: 6 changed mechanism to supports_activity(calculator, activity), 6 were reworded so the Protocol gains no mandatory member, and the two sites that describe a calculator DEFINING its own narrowing (the threshold-load cross-spec instruction, and the narrowing-only invariant) were left byte-identical and verified so by diff. A new bullet at the LoadContracts component records why the member form was rejected, so it is not re-proposed by a later spec. The SEMANTICS Amendment 3 specified are unchanged -- pure, prompt-free, athlete-data-free, asked before field collection, narrowing-only; only the call shape moved. CRITERION 8.7 RELAXED, NOT MERELY CLARIFIED -- FLAGGED FOR MAINTAINER RATIFICATION (2026-07-27, queue item 2026-07-26-req-87-offline-enumeration-stale, still `status: open` in `.kiro/queue/` -- closing is the human's call, this session only proposes it, per `.claude/skills/kiro-queue/SKILL.md:157`; no task reopened). CORRECTED characterization (2026-07-27, same review pass): this was first recorded as "a criterion clarification, no behavior change" -- that undersells what changed. The OLD 8.7 read "using only the data root's documents, archived sources, and the athlete profile" -- a RESTRICTIVE, closed enumeration that named three sources and implicitly excluded a fourth. Amendment 3's Req 14.4 (approved, `approvals.requirements.approved: true`) then required the load pass to read the `[load]` table exactly once per invocation as part of that same pass -- src/fitdocs/load/engine.py:260 does read fitdocs.toml today. Under the OLD 8.7's wording, that read was a VIOLATION: 8.7 and 14.4 contradicted each other, both already approved, with nothing flagging the conflict. This edit resolves that contradiction by RELAXING 8.7 -- widening its closed enumeration to a fourth item, "and its own resolved `[load]` configuration" (requirements.md:355; design.md's parallel LoadEngine enumeration, was line 1527-1528, amended in lockstep) -- rather than by narrowing Req 14.4 or reverting the shipped fitdocs.toml read. The resolution direction is very likely correct (14.4 is shipped and load-bearing; 8.7's three-item list reads like an oversight predating Amendment 3, not a deliberate exclusion of configuration). But it is a substantive relaxation of a previously-approved restrictive criterion, made with `approvals.requirements.approved` left `true` and no re-approval event recorded. THIS SESSION DOES NOT FLIP THAT APPROVAL FLAG. It is left exactly as the prior state, and this edit -- like the rest of this note -- awaits the maintainer's explicit ratification that relaxing 8.7 rather than re-scoping 14.4 was the right call. Three of training-load's own remaining `LoadCalculator.supports` references were repinned onto the module-level `supports_activity` (src/fitdocs/load/types.py:380), matching the ruling already recorded at design.md:815 and the repin already applied to threshold-load and activity-qa-flags by a24fcdf: design.md's revalidation trigger (was :292) now names the condition that can actually still occur -- supports_activity's resolution order changing -- rather than the removed Protocol member; design.md's Req 1.14 traceability row (was :682) now names `supports_activity`; and tasks.md's Amendment 3 summary (was :34) does the same. amendments.reason: The result contract was shaped around the only methodology that existed: its single point value plus 'zone', 'zone_label' and 'structure' is the withdrawn methodology's vocabulary. The Phase 4 threshold engine computes a load per available channel and selects one, so it has several values where the contract has one, a selection basis where the contract has a zone, and quality flags the contract cannot carry at all. The contract is therefore redefined rather than extended. Measured blast radius before deciding: 3 construction sites in src/, field reads confined to render.py and docedit.py, ~1,090 lines of directly shape-pinned tests, and zero generated documents carrying the load frontmatter keys.
amendments.also: Two behavioral decisions ratified by the user: the threshold engine is the default calculator when none is configured (Req 10.2), and frontmatter exposes only the selected value, methodology and basis while non-selected channel values and quality flags stay in the section payload (Req 7.2, 7.3). fitdocs is pre-production with no external plugin authors, so the plugin-author surface carries no backward-compatibility obligation and tests/test_public_api.py is repinned rather than frozen; plugin-api's compatibility statement must declare the surface unstable before 1.0. No existing requirement or criterion was renumbered -- engine.py cites 'Req 1.3, 8.4' in code comments and design.md/tasks.md reference these numbers throughout.
amendments.cross_spec: wiki-contract owns contract.py's LOAD_KEYS/MANAGED_KEYS and doc_version; its update must land with this one or a document that has had a load pass reports unmanaged keys. Requirement 12 is the regression guard that the withdrawn methodology survives the redefinition unchanged in both number and presentation.

amendments.requirement: Requirements 4, 5, 6 and 12 withdrawn; 1.5, 2.7, 3.6, 9.2 and 10.2 revised; Requirement 13 added
amendments.reason: The withdrawn methodology is withdrawn from fitdocs entirely. Three findings: (1) it produces no numbers in practice -- it requires per-activity interactive confirmation of zone and interval-vs-continuous structure, so any non-interactive pass yields NotConfirmed by design and a full rebuild over 71 real activities leaves every document uncomputed; (2) its tables and name require its author's permission before public redistribution, which was never obtained and gates any release of this repository; (3) zone/zone_label/structure are its vocabulary, so with it gone the Amendment 1 contract is defined for the multi-channel threshold engine rather than migrated from a single-channel one, and Requirement 12's continuity guarantee has nothing to guarantee.
amendments.also: Withdrawn requirements keep their numbers and are marked withdrawn in place; nothing is renumbered, so code, design and task citations of surviving requirements stay valid. This spec now ships NO calculator -- it is the carrier (contract, registry, arbitration, profile, prompt flow, document integration, load pass) and the first calculator is threshold-load's. Until that lands, no registered calculator supports any sport and every document correctly receives the Requirement 7.7 honest unsupported state; that interim is specified, not a regression. Requirement 13 covers the withdrawal itself, including 13.4: a document already carrying a result under the withdrawn methodology is left unchanged and reported skipped, never silently erased or misattributed.
amendments.decisions: Two behavioral decisions taken in this amendment and flagged for review. (1) Req 10.2 no longer names the threshold engine as the no-config default: with the withdrawn methodology gone the previously ratified 'default to threshold' would name an unregistered id and fail every install until threshold-load lands. It now reads: exactly one supporting calculator -> use it; several -> skip with a reason naming the candidates and directing the user to configure a default; never registration order. This resolves the R1 open question from the gap analysis and is correct at every stage of the roadmap. (2) Requirement 10 is REVISED, not withdrawn -- its load-bearing motivation is independent of the withdrawn methodology, because the retained plugin surface lets a third-party calculator silently displace a built-in by registration order (roadmap 296-300).
amendments.cross_spec: The plugin extension point is RETAINED; plugin-api continues to own the published surface, but its compatibility statement (docs/plugins.md:245-251) still promises additive-only change within 0.x and must be reconciled -- either a minor version bump plus the changelog it promises, or a declaration that the surface is unstable pre-1.0. threshold-load becomes the sole source of a built-in calculator and is now on the critical path for fitdocs computing any load at all. Steering (product.md, tech.md, structure.md, roadmap.md) presents the withdrawn methodology as the shipped methodology and needs updating. The reference writeup and extracted tables documenting the withdrawn methodology were research references, not shipped data. Their retention was reversed on 2026-07-30 (see the 2026-07-31 amendment below); they are removed, not retained.

amendments.requirement: 3.1 revised; 1.12, 1.13, 1.14, 1.15 added; Requirement 14 (14.1-14.6) added; 14.7 added 2026-07-25 by the import-direction correction below
amendments.reason: A cross-spec consistency review over the Phase 4 chain (athlete-benchmarks -> load-channels -> threshold-load -> activity-qa-flags) found four places where this spec's carrier is under-specified enough that four sibling specs each invented a different answer. (1) OWNERSHIP: src/fitdocs/load/settings.py does not exist yet and five specs claim it -- this spec creates it as load_load_settings(document, settings_file), athlete-benchmarks independently created it as load_settings_from_document(document, path), and three more said 'extend whichever exists', so the second lander would rename a public symbol. training-load is the owner; load_load_settings matches the dominant shipped convention (plugins.load_plugin_settings(document, settings_file), inbox.load_inbox_settings(document, *, data_root)) whereas load_settings_from_document follows the older tiles variant and collides confusingly with fitdocs.settings.load_settings_document, which reads the FILE. (2) WIRING: two incompatible reads of [load] were specified -- cli.py reading it and threading a lone default_calculator scalar into apply_load, versus apply_load reading it and owning the whole resolved LoadSettings. Landing both reads the document twice per invocation and leaves apply_load carrying a scalar that is already a member of the settings object it also holds. (3) CONTEXT: Amendment 1 left compute()'s parameter list unchanged, so a calculator has no route to its own configuration (channel priority, sufficiency thresholds, staleness window) or to the activity's date; three downstream specs each worked around this by parking per-pass state on ProfileView -- a protocol documented as a 'minimal read-only view of the athlete profile' -- which also inverts the types -> settings import direction and forces load/qa/__init__.py to be crippled so its own evaluate_flags is unreachable from the package root. (4) TWO CONTRACT CORRECTIONS: NotConfirmed is documented for a confirmation step Amendment 2 withdrew with Requirement 4 and has no producer in src/, while threshold-load is about to become its sole producer for the unrelated meaning 'no channel could be scored'; and LoadCalculator has no sport-level question, so threshold-load -- which must declare Modality.OTHER to reach Walk and Hike -- would drag Rowing and Workout documents through the entire interactive prompt flow before refusing them by sport.
amendments.also: RULINGS APPLIED. (1) load/settings.py is training-load's, with the pinned surface load_load_settings(document: Mapping[str, object], settings_file: Path) -> LoadSettings, LoadSettingsError(SettingsError), DEFAULT_LOAD_SETTINGS, and EVERY LoadSettings field defaulted (default_calculator: str | None = None, changed from undefaulted); unknown keys and unknown sub-tables are ignored so siblings add [load.sufficiency], [load.priority], [load.flags] and benchmark_staleness_days additively; siblings EXTEND the single dataclass and no second reader may exist (Requirement 14). (2) apply_load reads [load] once and owns the resolved LoadSettings; its default_calculator parameter is DELETED and --calculator remains the sole CLI override; SettingsError/LoadSettingsError now leave apply_load and reach the CLI's existing exit-2 handler. (3) compute() gains a fifth parameter: LoadContext(activity_date: date | None, settings: LoadSettings), frozen, built per activity by the engine; ProfileView reverts to a pure store view and must NOT carry activity_date, staleness_window_days or load_settings. This also moves settings.py BELOW types.py in the internal dependency order (settings -> types -> registry -> ...), which is what dissolves the cycle activity-qa-flags was dodging. activity_date is the document's own recorded LOCAL CALENDAR DATE, read from the already-parsed frontmatter through contract.document_date (athlete-benchmarks' accessor -- referenced, not respecified here): not a clock read, not a UTC instant, not a conversion of the activity's start timestamp, so the pass holds no time zone and cannot disagree with the document; an undated or unparseable document binds None and a calculator needing a date must decline rather than substitute today. (4a) NotConfirmed -> NotComputed with a rewritten docstring; engine.py:405's routing is already correct and unchanged. (4b) LoadCalculator gains supports(activity) -> bool, defaulting to the existing modality test, asked BEFORE the prompt flow; threshold-load implements it as activity.sport in SUPPORTED_SPORTS and its compute sport check becomes defence in depth. Legitimacy: the roadmap's ratified position (2026-07-25) that the pre-1.0 plugin-author surface carries no backward-compatibility obligation and that tests/test_public_api.py is repinned, not frozen -- the same basis Amendment 1 used. docs/contributing-calculators.md, the stub calculators, engine.py and load/__init__.py move with it. The canonical test module for the reader is pinned as tests/load/test_settings.py (suite convention tests/<package>/test_<module>.py; tests/load/test_packaging.py already coexists with tests/test_packaging.py, so the shared basename is precedent, not a collision).
amendments.decisions: KNOWN OPEN ITEM, user-deferred and explicitly out of scope: required_athlete_fields() remains activity-blind, so a calculator declares one field set for all activities. Consequence: a runner with no bicycle is asked for a cycling FTP on every interactive pass, and athlete-benchmarks Req 8.5 (a decline persists nothing) means the question repeats forever. supports(activity) narrows the blast radius to sports a calculator actually covers but does not close it. Recorded so the next spec to hit it inherits the finding. TASK-PLAN IMPACT: tasks 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 are COMMITTED and none is reopened -- 2.1 shipped LoadResult/NonSelectedValue/QualityFlag in final shape and Amendment 3 touches only the parts of load/types.py that 2.1 deliberately left alone. New task 3.3 (contract repin: LoadContext, supports, NotComputed, ProfileView purity) depends on 3.1 because LoadContext.settings is typed by LoadSettings -- so the previously independent contract and policy chains now share one edge. Task 3.1's scope grew to the pinned surface and total defaulting; task 4.1 absorbs the settings read plus the context construction and the supports call; task 4.2 shrank to keeping the command surface free of load configuration; task 5.1 now depends on 3.3; tasks 6.1 and 6.4 gained guards. Leaf tasks: 17 (was 16). Criteria: 68 (was 58).
amendments.cross_spec: athlete-benchmarks: has already been amended to conform AND now DEPENDS on this amendment landing -- it dropped activity_date and staleness_window_days from ProfileView (and with them AthleteProfile.for_activity and load_profile's window parameter), so LoadContext.activity_date is its only route to the activity date; it drops its own load/settings.py creation and the load_settings_from_document name and adds benchmark_staleness_days: int = 84 as a defaulted field on this spec's LoadSettings; it retains contract.document_date and the wiki-contract incursion that adds it, which MUST NOT interleave with task 2.4 (same module src/fitdocs/contract.py, same test module tests/test_contract.py, and 2.4 must be one atomic commit). load-channels: already conformant on the reader (its 2026-07-25 amendment pins this signature and extends LoadSettings with [load.sufficiency]); only its test-module name needs correcting. threshold-load: must read configuration from context.settings rather than ProfileView.load_settings, read the date from context.activity_date, implement supports(activity) as activity.sport in SUPPORTED_SPORTS with the compute sport check retained as defence in depth, and treat NotComputed as the variant it produces for 'no channel could be scored'. activity-qa-flags: must read [load.flags] from context.settings, drop ProfileView.load_settings as an inbound, and may un-cripple load/qa/__init__.py (the import cycle it was dodging does not exist under the settings -> types direction). All three of load-channels, threshold-load and activity-qa-flags must rename their test module to tests/load/test_settings.py. plugin-api: unchanged obligation from Amendment 1 -- the compatibility statement must declare the surface unstable pre-1.0, which is what makes a second contract redefinition legitimate; ALSO (2026-07-25) its published surface list still names NotConfirmed (plugin-api/design.md:806), which task 3.3's rename obsoletes -- task 5.2 reconciles both in one pass, editing none of plugin-api's files from here. activity-qa-flags (2026-07-25 correction): the sentence above telling it the cycle 'does not exist under the settings -> types direction' is WITHDRAWN as falsified; the cycle is real and is cut by the TYPE_CHECKING-only import in load/types.py instead, so that spec deletes its lazy __getattr__ re-export in load/qa/__init__.py and makes it an ordinary eager initializer. It is being amended in parallel.
amendments.correction: 2026-07-25, cross-spec import-direction ruling (BLOCKING review finding, applied without reopening committed work). Amendment 3 asserted at design.md:839-840 that load/settings.py 'has no fitdocs.load.* imports, which is what lets it sit below types.py'. FALSE, and contradicted by design.md:825-828 in the same component: LoadSettings aggregates SufficiencySettings (load/channels/types.py, load-channels), ChannelPriority (load/priority.py, threshold-load) and FlagSettings (load/qa/types.py, activity-qa-flags). A reviewer reproduced the cycle in a throwaway package mirroring the specified layout: fitdocs.load.types -> fitdocs.load.settings -> fitdocs.load.qa/__init__ -> fitdocs.load.qa.flags -> fitdocs.load.types (partial) -> ImportError, failing on import fitdocs.load.types, import fitdocs.load AND import fitdocs.load.qa, because src/fitdocs/load/__init__.py:17 imports registry which imports types. channels/ and priority.py escape only because nothing in them imports fitdocs.load.types (an invariant load-channels pins with a boundary test); qa/flags.py legitimately needs QualityFlag from load/types.py, so qa/ cannot. RULING: cut the one inverted edge with `if TYPE_CHECKING: from fitdocs.load.settings import LoadSettings` in load/types.py. settings.py returns above types.py and may import channels/types, priority and qa/types freely; every sub-package may import load.types; qa/__init__.py becomes an ordinary eager initializer. Two alternatives REJECTED on evidence and recorded so they are not re-proposed: (a) activity-qa-flags' lazy __getattr__ re-export -- the reviewer added one plausible future edge (a load/channels module importing fitdocs.load.types) and the lazy version failed immediately with the identical ImportError while the ruling passed, leaving the fragility load-bearing; (b) moving all sub-settings into load/settings.py -- SufficiencySettings.minimum_for needs ChannelId and ChannelPriority needs ChannelId + Sport, so settings.py would still import load/channels/types.py while the channel modules take settings: SufficiencySettings and import back, trading the cycle for a channels <-> settings one. This also RESTORES a shipped documented invariant Amendment 3 otherwise broke (src/fitdocs/load/types.py:3-9, 'the bottom of the load dependency chain ... no imports from other fitdocs.load.* modules'), which stays true at runtime and gains one sentence noting the type-checking-only exception in task 3.3.

amendments.requirement: None. No requirement or criterion is added, revised, withdrawn or renumbered -- all three corrections are design and task-plan defects measured against the requirements as they already stand (1.6, 1.12, 10.2, 14.7).
amendments.reason: A /kiro-validate-design pass over the spec after Amendment 3 and the import-direction correction. Three defects, all in pending work: (1) task 4.1 could not build a LoadContext because contract.document_date does not exist and lay outside its declared boundary; (2) arbitration's no-default candidate filter was modality-granular where Reqs 1.6 and 10.2 are sport-granular; (3) task 6.4's fresh-interpreter import guard named fitdocs.load.qa, which this spec does not create and which does not exist in the checkout.
amendments.also: RULINGS APPLIED. (1) DOCUMENT DATE: this spec lands first (verified: `document_date` resolves nowhere in src/ or tests/; athlete-benchmarks is at phase tasks-generated with zero committed tasks), so task 4.1 adds `document_date(frontmatter) -> date | None` to src/fitdocs/contract.py with tests in tests/test_contract.py, and its boundary reads `LoadEngine, DocumentContract (declared incursion: the document-date accessor only)`. It adds the accessor and nothing else -- the managed keys and DOC_VERSION were settled by task 2.4 (a782034). athlete-benchmarks becomes a pure consumer and must drop the incursion from its own plan. (2) ARBITRATION: `arbitrate` takes the activity rather than the bare modality, and its no-default branch narrows `registry.for_modality(activity.modality)` by `calculator.supports(activity)`. The forced-id and configured-default paths stay sport-blind -- that argument (Req 10.5 forbids substituting a different calculator for a declining one) was correct and is untouched. Purity is restated rather than relaxed: no filesystem, no document knowledge, no METHODOLOGY EXECUTION; `supports` is contractually prompt-free, athlete-data-free and side-effect-free (Req 1.14), so the module stays unit-testable without a filesystem. The engine's own support check stays UNCONDITIONAL, so the question is asked twice on the no-default path -- deliberate, and recorded as such so it is not optimized away: arbitration's use is candidate selection (1.6), the engine's is the single enforcement point for 3.1/7.7/10.5, which must hold identically for a forced or configured calculator arbitration never narrowed. Composability rests on `supports` being permitted only to NARROW a declared modality, so the registry prefilter can never drop a calculator `supports` would reinstate. (3) IMPORT GUARD: the guard enumerates the immediate sub-packages of fitdocs.load on disk and imports fitdocs.load, fitdocs.load.types, fitdocs.load.settings and each discovered sub-package, each in its own fresh subprocess. It stays a subprocess -- an in-process re-import is a sys.modules cache hit and proves nothing. Discovery is strictly better than a static list: channels/, priority and qa/ are covered the moment they land and no sibling spec edits this test, which is the coordination cost Req 14.7 exists to eliminate.
amendments.decisions: TASK-PLAN IMPACT. Task 3.2 now calls supports(), which task 3.3 adds to the contract, so 3.2 gains `_Depends: 1.3, 3.3_` and DROPS its (P) marker -- strict type checking would fail if the two ran concurrently. This costs nothing real: the concurrency 3.2 was granted was with major task 2, which is committed in full. Task 3.2 also gains three unit cases on the narrowing (two calculators declaring one modality: exactly one supports -> Selected; neither supports -> NoCalculator; both support -> sorted Ambiguous), task 4.1 gains the accessor and the activity-passing, task 6.1 gains the end-to-end two-broad-modality case (unsupported, not ambiguity), and task 6.4's guard is rewritten. Leaf tasks: 18, unchanged. Criteria: 69, unchanged. Nothing committed is reopened.
amendments.cross_spec: athlete-benchmarks: MUST DROP its contract.document_date incursion and become a pure consumer -- this spec's task 4.1 now adds the accessor with the signature that spec specified, so a second addition would conflict on src/fitdocs/contract.py and tests/test_contract.py. Everything else it owes is unchanged (it still depends on LoadContext.activity_date as its only route to the activity date, and still extends LoadSettings with benchmark_staleness_days). threshold-load: unaffected in obligation but DIRECTLY BENEFITS -- its Modality.OTHER declaration for Walk and Hike is exactly the shape that made the modality-granular filter wrong, and the narrowing means a Rowing or Workout document now reaches the honest unsupported state instead of an unresolvable ambiguity once a second OTHER-declaring calculator exists. activity-qa-flags, load-channels: unaffected; the discovered-sub-package guard means neither needs to edit tests/test_public_api.py when its package lands. plugin-api: unchanged obligations from Amendments 1-3.

amendments.reason: The encumbered-content-purge spec reversed a retention ruling this spec's design.md and tasks.md recorded for the reference writeup and extracted tables documenting the withdrawn methodology. Those materials were retained as a research record of the withdrawal. That retention was reversed on 2026-07-30 because publishing this repository would publish them. The reversal is declared here as a cross-boundary correction against this already-implemented spec, not as a reopening of it.
amendments.also: The original retention was a decision taken under the circumstances then in force, not an error corrected here. The methodology's author is not named by this entry or by the corrected sites. design.md's withdrawal component and its Out of Boundary list, tasks.md's task 5.2 bullet, and this entry's own sibling amendment (index 1, cross_spec) are corrected in place to record the reversal in place of the original retention instruction; none of the four sites is deleted, and this correction touches no checkbox, no approval boolean, no phase value and no readiness value.
